claim: The authors observed no effect of pre-pubertal castration on mouse lifespan.
source: In contrast, we observed no effect of pre-pubertal castration on mouse lifespan
evidence: This claim is supported by survival data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The findings differ from results previously reported for rats and humans regarding castration effects on lifespan.
source: Our findings differ from results previously reported for rats and humans (Drori and Folman, 1976; Min et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is based on comparison with prior literature.

claim: Previous studies on castration and lifespan may have been impacted by effects of castration on rodent aggression or confounded by the social status of the castrated humans.
source: but these studies may have been impacted by effects of castration on rodent aggression or confounded by the social status of the castrated humans
evidence: This claim is based on speculation about confounding factors in prior studies.

claim: Hormone replacement promotes the survival of men with late onset hypogonadism.
source: Conversely, hormone replacement promotes the survival of men with late onset hypogonadism (Comhaire, 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The results do not support a model in which ablation of the male germline is beneficial for healthspan or longevity.
source: Our results do not support a model in which ablation of the male germline is beneficial for healthspan or longevity
evidence: This claim is based on the lack of positive effects of castration on survival and metabolic health.

claim: The authors observed an effect of castration on weight and body composition in agreement with recent studies by other groups.
source: In agreement with recent studies by other groups (Garratt et al., 2017; Harada et al., 2016; Inoue et al., 2010), we observed an effect of castration on weight and body composition
evidence: This claim is supported by body composition data shown in Figure 3 and citations to prior literature.

claim: The authors did not observe an effect of castration on glucose homeostasis.
source: but did not observe an effect of castration on glucose homeostasis
evidence: This claim is supported by glucose tolerance test data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: A limitation of this study is that the authors did not perform a comprehensive assessment of healthspan.
source: A limitation of this study is that we did not perform a comprehensive assessment of healthspan (Bellantuono et al., 2020), focusing instead on metabolic parameters
evidence: This claim acknowledges a limitation of the study design.

claim: Pre-pubertal ovariectomy uncouples metabolic health and survival, as in the case of C. elegans where lifespan and healthspan can be uncoupled.
source: Despite this, it is clear that as in the case of C. elegans, where lifespan and healthspan can be uncoupled (Bansal et al., 2015), pre-pubertal ovariectomy uncouples metabolic health and survival
evidence: This claim is supported by the observation of improved survival despite impaired metabolic health, and comparison with prior literature.

claim: There is a broad consensus in favor of extending healthspan.
source: as while there is a broad consensus in favor of extending healthspan
evidence: This claim is based on general scientific consensus.

claim: There is less support for extending lifespan without extending healthspan.
source: there is less support for extending lifespan without extending healthspan (Kaeberlein, 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The research highlights the need to comprehensively assess the effects of geroprotectors on healthspan.
source: Our research here highlights the need to comprehensively assess the effects of geroprotectors on healthspan, as at least some aspects of healthspan are not inextricably coupled to longevity
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the findings that metabolic health and longevity can be uncoupled.

claim: At least some aspects of healthspan are not inextricably coupled to longevity.
source: as at least some aspects of healthspan are not inextricably coupled to longevity
evidence: This claim is supported by the observation that ovariectomized mice have improved survival despite impaired metabolic health.

claim: Cancer was observed in approximately half of the necropsied animals.
source: As we expected for C57BL/6J mice (Brayton et al., 2012), we observed cancer in approximately half of the necropsied animals
evidence: This claim is supported by necropsy data and is consistent with expectations for this mouse strain.

claim: There was no statistically significant difference in the frequency of observed cancer at necropsy between groups of male mice (chi-square test, p=0.06).
source: There was no statistically significant difference in the frequency of observed cancer at necropsy between groups of male mice (chi-square test, p=0.06)
evidence: This claim is supported by chi-square analysis of necropsy data.

claim: Cancer was identified much more frequently in L-RKO CAST mice than in any other group of male mice.
source: although cancer was identified much more frequently in L-RKO CAST mice than in any other group of male mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by necropsy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mice hemizygous for Albumin-Cre and homozygous for a floxed allele of Rictor were obtained by crossing RictorL/L mice with Albumin-Cre mice.
source: Mice hemizygous for Albumin-Cre and homozygous for a floxed allele of Rictor mice were obtained by crossing RictorL/L mice on a C57BL/6J background (Lamming et al., 2012), obtained from the Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research (Cambridge, MA) and rederived by embryo transfer at the UW-Madison Biotechnology Center, with Albumin-Cre mice (The Jackson Laboratory, Stock 003574 Postic et al., 1999)
evidence: This claim describes the breeding strategy used to generate the experimental mice.

claim: Mice were gonadectomized or subject to sham surgery during the third week of age.
source: Mice were gonadectomized or subject to sham surgery during the third week of age
evidence: This claim describes the timing of the surgical intervention.

claim: A total of 115 female and 105 male mice were included in the lifespan study.
source: A total of 115 female and 105 male mice were included in the lifespan study, with 23 female and 22 male mice removed for cross sectional analysis
evidence: This claim describes the sample size of the study.

claim: 23 female and 22 male mice were removed for cross sectional analysis.
source: A total of 115 female and 105 male mice were included in the lifespan study, with 23 female and 22 male mice removed for cross sectional analysis
evidence: This claim describes mice that were censored from the survival analysis.

claim: Mice were co-housed (grouped by sex and surgical intervention) in specific pathogen-free housing.
source: Mice were co-housed (grouped by sex and surgical intervention) in specific pathogen-free housing
evidence: This claim describes the housing conditions for the mice.

claim: During gross necropsy, the abdominal and thoracic cavities were examined for the presence of solid tumors, metastases, splenomegaly, and infection.
source: Mice found dead were noted at each daily inspection and saved in a refrigerator for gross necropsy, during which the abdominal and thoracic cavities were examined for the presence of solid tumors, metastases, splenomegaly, and infection
evidence: This claim describes the necropsy procedure.

claim: Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed separately for each sex using genotype and surgical treatment as covariates.
source: Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed separately for each sex using genotype and surgical treatment as covariates
evidence: This claim describes the statistical analysis method used.
